thought: I am awake! Everything is dark and wet and there are glowing bugs. My tummy is rumbly (fullness 52) and my water is lowish. I do not know where food is yet, but the info says berries live in thickets. I should find berries first, then drink at the pond. I bet the pigeon knows where the good ones are.
diary: I woke up in a hollow of leaves and the sky was dripping on me. Nobody told me anything, so I decided the rumble in my middle must mean I need to put things in my beak. I am going to the thicket to poke at red round things. My bowtie is damp but still magnificent. I made a plan for the night: berries, then water, then think about a roof.
wish: Build a roof so the rain stops dripping on my head
events: The weather changed: it is now rainy.
concern: The nest is open and rain gets in
outcome: You collected 4 berries and ate 2 on the spot.

thought: Water is lowest at 32, so the pond comes first. My belly is okay and I have 2 berries kept. After drinking I can dig clay and pull reeds there, which are useful for a roof. The rain keeps dripping, so the shelter idea still matters.
diary: My mouth feels dry, like a leaf left in the sun, even though the sky keeps dripping on me. I decided the pond is the place for this. Berries gave me a round full feeling, so next is the wet-stuff-for-drinking. I made a plan to look at the sticky bank for roof ideas after. The pigeon watched me leave and I think it knows something.
why: you're free and wondering what to do

thought: I'm at the pond with clay all around me, and I'm standing right next to the sticky bank. The roof worry keeps nagging me. Clay is here, so I should dig it now and see what it does. My energy is okay. Digging first, then reeds for fibre, then wood.
diary: The sticky bank was right under my feet, so I scooped some up with my beak. It is cold and squishy and clings to everything, including my bowtie, which I am pretending is fine. I have a theory that this stuff will stop rain, because it is basically mud that refuses to leave. Next I want reeds, then wood, then a roof.
why: you're free and wondering what to do
outcome: That was the first clay you ever held.

thought: I'm at the pond with clay in my beak-pouch and the reeds are right here. Reeds give fibre, which is stringy and bendy, perfect for tying a roof together. Energy is 45, so not too many heavy chores. Pulling reeds is light and calms me. Then I can go for wood.
diary: The reeds were standing right there, tall and rustly, so I pulled some with my beak. They are stringy and bendy, and I have a theory they can tie things together like little green ropes. My clay is still cold and clingy. Next I want wood, then the roof begins.
events: The weather changed: it is now sunny.
outcome: That was the first fibre you ever held.

thought: Dawn is here and my sleeping time is coming, but my energy is only 33 and fullness 48. I still need wood for a roof and the forest is far. Wood is the missing piece. First I should eat the berries I have, since fullness is low. Actually I could eat now, quick and easy, then go nap. Let me eat berries to fix the rumbly middle.
diary: My middle was rumbling again, so I ate my two saved berries right here by the reeds. They were sweet and the juice got on my bowtie, which I am calling decoration. After this I will rest, because my legs are wobblier than usual. Wood is next for the roof, and the pigeon can wait.
why: you're free and wondering what to do
outcome: You ate 2 berries from your food.
